nodes.name: Webhook
nodes.notes: Consumer (queue-consumer, ADR-056) POSTs here over the INTERNAL docker network (http://n8n-main:5678/webhook/spine-ingress), bypassing nginx's 300s proxy_read_timeout. responseMode=responseNode holds the connection for the whole spine run (up to 15 min, G5) and replies via the Respond node. The held HTTP response IS the authoritative spine-result signal — the consumer classifies from it, NOT by polling agent_runs (Block 0 G2).

nodes.name: Run Agent Orchestrator
nodes.notes: Runs the Agent Orchestrator (a8XKaijkMFNBpRBa) inline, holding the webhook connection. onError=continueErrorOutput routes a thrown spine error to output 1 (-> Build Outcome (failed)) instead of bubbling a 500. alwaysOutputData=true guarantees output 0 carries >=1 item even when the orchestrator's branchy terminal returns 0 items (the n8n sub-workflow-return-determinism trap that produced the Block 0 'No item to return' 500) — so Build Outcome (completed) always has an item to coalesce. Maps the 7 spine inputs from the webhook body verbatim (unchanged from Block 0, which drove a real spine end-to-end).

nodes.name: Build Outcome (completed)
nodes.notes: Coalesces the success branch to ONE deterministic outcome item, independent of what the orchestrator's non-deterministic terminal returned. If the orchestrator happened to return its structured outcome ({status,outcome,failure_kind,warnings} from Call Execute Agent Session) those pass through; otherwise they default (status->completed, since the orchestrator ran without throwing). clickup_task_id is read from the Webhook body (always present). This shape is the consumer's classification contract (Block 0 G2 / Block 2).

nodes.name: Build Outcome (failed)
nodes.notes: The orchestrator threw and onError routed here. Returns status=failed + failure_kind=orchestrator_exception + the error message as a deterministic 200 body (NOT an HTTP 5xx) so the consumer's HTTP client / BullMQ don't auto-retry a business failure (double-draft guard, Block 0 G2). The consumer (Block 2) classifies retryable-vs-DLQ from failure_kind + the message; genuine transport/timeout/n8n-5xx failures never reach here (the HTTP call itself fails) and are the consumer's retryable-infra path.

nodes.name: Respond to Webhook
nodes.notes: Single deterministic terminal for both branches (success XOR error -> exactly one item arrives). Always HTTP 200; the business outcome lives in the body's status field. This is what makes the held HTTP response an authoritative, deterministic spine-result signal (fixes the Block 0 bare-lastNode 500).
